title: Christian emigration from Mount Lebanon begins after 1860 conflict
why: First large outward wave; seeds a diaspora now larger than the resident population.

title: Last official census counts about 793,000 residents
why: Sect ratios from it still anchor power-sharing; no census since, since new numbers could upset the balance.

title: Beirut becomes Arab publishing hub: 39 newspapers, 137 periodicals
why: Free-press reputation still invoked today (date corrected from 1950s: the page places these counts in the 1940s).

title: National Pact sets 6:5 sect quotas based on 1932 census
why: Pact introduced 7 Oct 1943; Christian-to-Muslim ratio 6:5 rests on the 1932 count, which is why a new census is avoided.

title: Pre-war emigration small: 3,000, 8,000 and 10,000 per period
why: 1945-60, 1960-70, 1970-75 counts from the AUB page; the later waves dwarf them.

title: First Labour Code issued after union general strike
why: State recognises trade unions; later labour and social-insurance fights build on it.

title: Palestinian refugees reach Lebanon after 1948 war (Lebanon count unverified)
why: About 700,000-750,000 Palestinians were displaced overall; the often-cited 110,000 for Lebanon was not confirmed on a page I opened.

title: UNRWA begins operations serving Palestine refugees
why: Created by UN resolution 302 on 8 Dec 1949; operations began 1950 (date corrected from 1950-05-01, day not confirmed).

title: Lebanese University founded after student strike
why: Only public university, created so lower-income Lebanese could study; its funding fight continues.

title: General strike forces President Khoury to resign
why: Widespread demonstrations by an opposition front forced resignation; Chamoun succeeded (date corrected from 1952-09).

title: Women obtain the right to vote (initially with schooling condition)
why: Condition of elementary education lifted in 1957; sources also cite 1952 agreement (date corrected from 1953-02-18).

title: Population estimated at 1.41 million
why: Baseline for the post-independence boom years before refugee inflows and civil war.

title: Schooling condition on women's vote lifted
why: Five years after the initial grant; Myrna Bustani became first woman MP in 1963.

title: Five-month civil crisis pits Maronite and Muslim camps
why: First post-independence sectarian confrontation; ended with Chehab reconciliation on 25 Oct and US withdrawal.

title: Television launched with two private stations
why: Media born private and politically patronised; merged into Tele Liban in 1977.

title: Confessional demographic-growth differences fuel census taboo
why: Perceived shifts in sect shares made a new census politically unthinkable; inference from the census avoidance record.

title: Press law regulates Lebanon's liberal media
why: The 1962 law still governs publishing, despite later criminal-defamation use against critics.

title: National Social Security Fund created by Chehab decree
why: Created by Decree 13955 under Chehab, bypassing parliamentary opposition; later gutted by devaluation (date corrected from 1963-09-30, day not confirmed).

title: Post-Six-Day-War Lebanese emigration to Australia rises
why: Reached 33,000 by 1976; shows emigration as a recurring pressure valve from the 1960s.

title: Further Palestinian arrivals after the Naksa
why: Plausible growth of camp populations after 1967; not confirmed on a page I opened.

title: Cairo Agreement formalises Palestinian presence
why: Later annulled; its legacy is the state's ambivalence toward camps and their legal status.

title: Pre-war Palestinian refugee population about 400,000
why: Sizeable, poorly integrated population entering the decade that ended in war.

title: Ghandour factory wildcat strike repressed by army
why: Strike began 3 Nov; on 11 Nov security forces dispersed workers, killing two (Youssef al-Attar, Fatema Khaweja).

title: Tobacco farmers' strike against Regie; army kills two
why: One of the largest pre-war strikes, part of the rural and worker protest wave before 1975.

title: Civil-war exodus: roughly 990,000 leave Lebanon
why: One estimate; other sources give 600,000 to 900,000. Established emigration as a reflex in crisis.

title: Sidon fishermen strike; Maarouf Saad fatally wounded
why: Protest against Chamoun-linked fishing monopoly; Saad shot 26 Feb, died 6 Mar; funeral became mass protest (date corrected from 1975-02).

title: Civil war begins; population about 2.7 million
why: Fifteen-year war: around 120,000 dead and nearly one million displaced.

title: Karantina and Damour massacres mark early sectarian displacement
why: Listed among first-phase events; war displaced nearly one million overall. Regional displacement figures not found.

title: About 990,000 leave during civil war, 40% of population
why: AUB data page figure; other sources give 600,000 to 900,000.

title: Tel al-Zaatar camp massacre
why: Camps became battlegrounds; the trauma still shapes Palestinian and Lebanese relations.
deaths: about 1,500 on 12 Aug 1976; 2,000-3,000 over the siege and massacre

title: Two private TV stations merged into Tele Liban
why: Wartime broadcasting fragmented along militia lines afterwards.

title: Sabra and Shatila camp massacres
why: Mass killing of Palestinian and Lebanese civilians; central to memory politics and missing-persons demands.

title: Israeli invasion begins; Sabra and Shatila killings follow in September
why: Siege of Beirut preceded PLO evacuation; Sabra-Shatila toll estimated 800 to 3,500 (displacement totals not confirmed).

title: Lebanese Forces launch LBC television station
why: Started 1985 as a militia station; became LBCI in 1992; example of wartime party media.

title: War of the Camps: sieges of Palestinian camps to July 1988
why: Official toll 3,781 dead and 6,787 injured in Amal-Palestinian fighting, probably undercounted.

title: Pound starts collapsing: LL 500 in 1987, over LL 2,500 by 1992
why: Wartime currency collapse wiped out savings; 900 per dollar in Dec 1989.

title: Taif Agreement rebalances representation to 50:50
why: Ends war framework, keeps confessional quotas without a new census.

title: War ends; population estimated about 3.3 to 3.6 million
why: Legacy of trauma, missing persons and divided communities. (corrected from about 3.6 million: CIA World Factbook 1990 gives 3,339,331; UN-based series about 3.6 million)

title: General amnesty for wartime crimes
why: Amnesty law left families of the disappeared without answers; the memory gap persists.

title: LBCI formed from wartime LBC assets
why: Postwar rebranding of militia media into a commercial broadcaster; ownership remained concentrated.

title: Cholera outbreak of 1993 is Lebanon's last before 2022
why: WHO and Wikipedia both call 2022 the first outbreak since 1993; no detail on 1993 found.

title: Lebanese newspapers go online
why: Among earliest Arab adopters of internet media; foundation for 2019 social-media organising.

title: LBC launches satellite channel LBCsat
why: Wartime Lebanese Forces station (1985) became LBCI in 1992, then reached diaspora worldwide; example of party-born media going global.

title: Grapes of Wrath displaces about 400,000; Qana shelling kills about 105
why: Two-week operation, 11-27 April; Qana UN compound hit 18 April; HRW counts about 154 Lebanese civilians killed.

title: Israeli occupation of south Lebanon ends
why: Returning communities resettled; southern social life reoriented around border tensions.

title: Law bars Palestinians from owning property
why: Legal discrimination deepened camp poverty and exclusion for decades.

title: Rafic Hariri assassinated
why: Triggered the largest peaceful mobilisation since the war.

title: Martyrs' Square rally; organisers claim over a million
why: Cross-sect anti-Syria crowd after 8 March pro-Syria rally; counts disputed on both sides.

title: Syrian troops complete withdrawal
why: Ended about 29 years of Syrian military presence; social resentment toward Syrian workers lingered.

title: Journalist Samir Kassir killed by car bomb
why: Al-Nahar columnist who helped trigger the Cedar upheaval; part of a 2004-2008 wave of killings of critics.

title: 34-day war displaces about one million
why: Fighting 12 July to 14 August; 1,191 to 1,300 Lebanese killed by varying counts; about one million displaced.

title: Nahr al-Bared battle: army takes camp on 2 September
why: Camp of about 30,000 residents mostly fled; by 2015 only about 5,857 lived there (date corrected from 2007).

title: Labour amendments eased Palestinian work permits
why: Partial reform but most Palestinians still work informally.

title: Syrian war begins; refugee arrivals start
why: Open-border phase brought roughly 1.5 million Syrians by some estimates, peaking past one million registered.

title: Anti-sectarian march of about 8,000 to Martyrs' Square
why: Largest anti-sectarian rally since the war; slogan to topple the sectarian regime.

title: Parliament repeals honour-killing sentence reduction
why: Page calls it Article 562 (some sources say 522); a rare legal win for women's rights campaigners.

title: Monetary poverty stands at 12% in 2012
why: World Bank baseline; poverty more than tripled to 44% by 2022 (the 25% figure for 2019 was not on the page).

title: Parliament passes domestic-violence law 293
why: Parliament passed a full domestic-violence law (date corrected from 2014-04-01, day not confirmed on a page I opened).

title: Remittances estimated at $8.9bn, 18% of economy
why: Family transfers cushioned households; later crises made emigrant support a social lifeline.

title: Literacy rate 97.9%
why: High literacy remains a social asset even as school attendance drops since 2019.

title: UNHCR registers over one million Syrian refugees
why: Largest per-capita refugee load worldwide; strain on schools, health and wages.

title: UNHCR told to stop registering new Syrian refugees
why: Drove many into irregular legal status; numbers declined from peak of about 1.2 million.

title: Naameh landfill closes; waste crisis erupts
why: Trash piles sparked the YouStink movement over governance failures.

title: YouStink rally draws over 100,000
why: Largest protest of the decade; 22-23 Aug clashes left 402 wounded and one dead.

title: Beirut Madinati takes about 32% of the vote in Beirut municipal election
why: Civic list born of protest showed an opening for non-sectarian politics. (corrected from 'wins about 40%': about 32% of ballots, nearly 40% excluding blank and spoiled; the list won no seats)

title: Census counts 174,422 Palestinians in camps and gatherings
why: Far below UNRWA's registered figure of about 489,000 (2023), a long-running numbers dispute.

title: Labour ministry's work-permit drive for foreign workers sparks Palestinian protests
why: Shows how labour enforcement collides with stateless residents' livelihood.

title: Thawra begins after WhatsApp tax; hundreds of thousands march
why: Largest cross-sect uprising since 2005: 'all of them means all of them'.

title: 171 km human chain from Tripoli to Tyre
why: Symbol of cross-regional solidarity; 11 protest deaths and 1,488 injured overall.

title: Hariri resigns 29 October after protests
why: Cabinet fell within two weeks of the uprising; 10 MPs also resigned over the following period.

title: NSSF end-of-service claims pile up
why: 32,959 indemnity requests pending Jan 2019 to Apr 2020; about 81% of NSSF assets frozen or in worthless bonds.

title: First COVID-19 case confirmed
why: Case was a 45-year-old woman returning from Qom; pandemic layered onto the financial collapse.

title: Beirut port blast kills 218, injures 7,000+
why: About 300,000 made homeless; hospitals destroyed; volunteers led the clean-up before the state did.

title: Diab cabinet resigns after blast protests
why: Public anger forced government change; accountability for the blast remains unresolved.

title: New standard contract for migrant domestic workers
why: Labour ministry contract: terminate without consent, keep ID and phone; about 250,000 workers remain under kafala (date corrected from 2020-09).

title: Order of Physicians: over 2,500 doctors had left by 2021
why: Mostly aged 35 to 55; the WHO 40%/30% estimate and nurse numbers were not confirmed on an opened page.

title: 2021: 79,134 emigrants, 4.5 times the 2020 number
why: AUB data page calls the post-2019 outflow Lebanon's most severe emigration wave (earlier 195,433 figure not found).

title: January 2021 COVID surge overwhelms hospitals; lockdown from 7 January
why: Curfew and lockdown ran 7 Jan to 8 Feb 2021 with few beds available (earlier death-count claim dropped as unconfirmed).

title: Publisher Lokman Slim found shot dead
why: Found shot dead in his car 3-4 Feb; case closed May 2021 with no arrests; no charges by Feb 2024.

title: Most medicine subsidies lifted
why: Cancer, mental-health and hospital drugs kept subsidies; prices rose up to fivefold or sixfold (date corrected: article dated 16 Nov, not 9 Nov).

title: Monetary poverty 44%; nearly 80% multidimensional (HRW citing World Bank)
why: HRW 2026 report repeats these figures; Palestinian refugees about 93% in poverty.

title: Enrolment fell from 60% to 43% (UNICEF)
why: UNICEF-attributed decline from 60% to 43%; the source page would not open, so unconfirmed.

title: Election: diaspora turnout 63%, national turnout 49%
why: 142,041 of 225,277 registered voters abroad voted; Hezbollah and allies lost their majority (13 change MPs and 8 women claims unconfirmed here).

title: Interior minister bans LGBTI-related events
why: Mawlawi ordered a ban on Pride events; the Shura Council suspended it on 1 Nov 2022.

title: Cholera returns; first outbreak since 1993
why: Index case 5 Oct; 5,105 cases and 23 deaths by 9 Dec; declared over June 2023 (date corrected from 2022-10-04).

title: Public schools frozen by teacher strike
why: Extended strike from 20 Dec 2022; teacher pay down over 90% since 2019 (about $50 a month); nearly 350,000 pupils affected.

title: Two-thirds of pupils attend private schools
why: Public schooling dominated by private provision, making the 2019+ public-school collapse acute for poorer families.

title: Hezbollah leader calls for action against gay people
why: HRW: Nasrallah called for action 'by all means necessary'; LGBT residents reported death threats afterwards.

title: Parliament adopts private-sector pension system
why: Replaces end-of-service indemnity after about three decades of attempts; ILO provided technical help (date corrected from 2023).

title: World Bank: poverty more than tripled in a decade
why: World Bank: 12% in 2012 to 44% in 2022; Akkar 70%; about 89% of Syrian households below the line.

title: Over one million displaced by late September 2024
why: UN, 30 Sept: 90% fled in the last week; displacement surpassed 2006 (1.2 million and 3,402 deaths not confirmed here).

title: Assad falls; Syrian returns accelerate
why: About 440,000 crossed to Syria by Oct 2024, many after Israeli strikes; returns climbed after December.

title: Syrian returns: about 379,000 to 400,000 (UNHCR); 500,000+ (government)
why: Gap in counts reflects who is removed from UNHCR records; needs care in citing.

title: More than 220,000 people leave Lebanon in a year
why: IOM-attributed figure; youth intent to leave 58% of 18-29s in 2024 Arab Barometer. (IOM figure is net border departures in 2025, about 2.63m entries vs 2.85m departures, per The Beiruter)

title: First municipal elections in nearly ten years, 4-24 May
why: Turnout 39% against 48.54% in 2016; four weekend rounds (women's results not confirmed) (date corrected from 2025-05).

title: Private-sector minimum wage set at LBP 28 million
why: About $312 a month, up from LBP 18 million in 2024 (date corrected from 2025-08-01: page cites June 2025 decree).

title: About 64,000 still displaced a year after 2024 ceasefire
why: IOM figure (64,417 per HRW) a year on from the Nov 2024 ceasefire; south remains unsafe and aid is thin.

title: Nationality law still bars mothers passing citizenship
why: Men pass it to children and foreign wives; opponents cite demographic balance; 2015 draft reform refused.

title: UNHCR and IOM organised returns continue with bigger luggage allowance
why: 8 cubic metres of luggage and a $100 per person cash grant; the 57,444 returnee figure was not confirmed here.

title: Six more public-sector salaries take effect
why: Cabinet approves six extra salaries on the 2019 wage scale, about $800m; effective date not stated (date corrected from 2026-03-01).

title: War resumes 2 March; over one million displaced
why: About one fifth of the population; 886 killed by mid-March per WHO (registered total 1,049,328 not confirmed here).

title: Parliament extends own mandate by two years
why: Vote 76 to 41 with four abstentions; new election due May 2028; Bassil called it the worst form of democracy.

title: Lebanese University Hadath campus struck; two professors killed
why: Schools and campuses became shelters or targets, compounding an education crisis.

title: World Bank: Lebanese poverty about 36% in 2025
why: World Bank Macro Poverty Outlook April 2026: headcount poverty among Lebanese in five governorates eased from about 37% in 2024 to 36% in 2025.

title: CPJ: at least seven journalists killed in Lebanon by 8 April
why: Includes two killed on 8 April; three more died in a strike on a press car on 28 March.

title: Ceasefire from 16-17 April, extended 23 April and 15 May
why: Fragile with violations; a separate truce dated 19 June in coordinator fact-check, while the New Arab cites 21 June.

title: MSF: 110 health workers killed since 2 March
why: 163 attacks on emergency crews, 16 hospitals hit; relayed by Press TV (state-linked), so treat with care (date corrected from 2026-03).

title: More than 464,000 cross-border movements into Syria since 2 March (as of 22 June, DTM)
why: Claimed 464,562 cross-border Syrian movements since 2 March; the UNHCR PDF could not be read.

title: IOM: 646,107 displaced begin returning; about 500,000 remain
why: Report published 3 July, data since 22 June; many border towns inaccessible (date corrected from 2026-06-22).

title: Al Jazeera: about 330,000 still displaced; 50+ border villages occupied
why: Peak 1.2 million in April; over 4,380 killed; returns fragile without rebuilding.

title: Planned transport and union mobilisation suspended after talks
why: Transport unions suspended after a finance-ministry aid deal for drivers (1 Oct to 31 Dec); public-administration staff continued striking.
